page: Microsoft Azure E192is_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance based on the x86_64 Intel processor architecture, managed through Microsoft Hyper-V. The system provides 192 dedicated virtual CPUs and 1832.0 GB of system memory, yielding an allocation of 9.54 GB of RAM per vCPU. As an isolated instance type, it runs on hardware dedicated entirely to a single tenant, mitigating multi-tenant resource contention. The server does not contain any integrated GPUs.

The instance comes without local storage, requiring all persistent and scratch disk operations to rely on remote networked block storage via Premium Storage. In terms of cost efficiency, the dedicated physical footprint and large memory allocation represent an infrastructure profile focused on scale-up density rather than ephemeral distributed tasks. The trade-off centers on the complete absence of ephemeral local NVMe disks, shifting I/O operations entirely to network-attached storage volumes.

Given its 1.8 TB memory footprint and dedicated 192 vCPUs, the E192is_v6 is suited for large-scale enterprise workloads such as in-memory databases, heavy transactional database systems, massive extract-transform-load data pipelines, and in-memory analytical compute jobs that demand full host isolation and high thread concurrency.
description: Microsoft Azure E192is_v6 is an isolated, memory-optimized virtual machine built on x86_64 Intel processor architecture and running under Microsoft Hyper-V. The configuration supplies 192 dedicated virtual CPUs paired with 1832.0 GB of system memory, delivering approximately 9.54 GB of RAM per vCPU without hardware GPU acceleration. It includes no integrated local storage, requiring attached Premium Storage volumes to handle persistent storage and application files. Running as an isolated instance, it allocates the full physical host to prevent multi-tenant interference. This architecture is designed for scale-up computing where massive shared memory and high CPU thread concurrency are essential. Economically, it trades away ephemeral local drive performance in favor of centralized storage management and dedicated host compute density. The server is suited for enterprise in-memory databases, large-scale enterprise resource planning platforms, extensive relational databases, and high-throughput data processing tasks.
